audit.why: Even poke lane early, Vex tilts at 6 and one item vs an immobile scaler; matches 49.19% WR and packet chart.
Spikes correctly listed: 3-5 poke war, 6 Shadow Surge, first item, late. Content spikes have 4 entries.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content layer uses Viktor's pre-rework ability names: 'Death Ray' (really Hextech Ray) and 'Chaos Storm' (really Arcane Storm). tradeGood/dosFull claim Viktor 'answers with a dash' and that trades 'schedule the next fear' off his dashes — Viktor has no dash, so Vex's passive mark-on-dash never triggers off him. Missing interaction: his combo opens with the Siphon Power (Q) auto-reset shield.
audit.why: Kit file is authority: E = Hextech Ray, R = Arcane Storm (channel-flagged, interruptible). Q is flagged autoReset + shield.
audit.corrected: Renamed abilities; rewrote trade lines around his Q shield cycle (9/8/7/6/5s) and Gravity Field (17-13s); noted the Q auto-reset as the burst tell.
Added Gravity Field 17-13s, Q 9-5s, own W 16s, R 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart: full phases[4..6].side said Skill/Skill/Viktor while content win[4..6] and the packet chart say Vex, and every why on those rows describes Vex winning.
audit.why: Two layers disagreed; packet levelChart and prose agree on Vex.

edits.before: This early lane is a skill-matched poke war: your charged Q trades with his Death Ray (E), and he shields with Siphon Power (Q) before empowering an auto. Manage the wave so he can't free-farm with E, and dodge his Gravity Field (W) zone if he tries to zone you. Neither of you has a clean kill yet, so it comes down to who lands more poke and respects mana.
edits.after: This early lane is a skill-matched poke war: your charged Q trades with his Hextech Ray (E, 12s at rank 1), and he shields with Siphon Power (Q) before empowering an auto — that reset wind-up is your cue to step back. Manage the wave so he can't free-farm with E, and walk out of Gravity Field (W) the moment it drops. Neither of you has a clean kill yet, so land poke and respect mana.

edits.before: Shadow Surge flips the lane your way: you now have a long-range engage and a fear that interrupts his Chaos Storm (R) channel. Wait for him to commit E or step up, then R-E to lock him — he's immobile and can't kite your all-in once feared. This is where the even lane starts tilting in your favor.
edits.after: Shadow Surge flips the lane your way: you now have a long-range engage and a fear that interrupts his Arcane Storm (R). Wait for him to commit E or step up, then R-E to lock him — he's immobile and can't kite your all-in once feared. This is where the even lane starts tilting in your favor.

edits.before: Viktor is a monster if he free-scales, but you hold the pick initiative: your R range and fear open on him from angles his Gravity Field can't cover, and the fear cancels his Chaos Storm before it does work. Face him, hold E to interrupt, and blow him up before he kites. Deny his farm and the game stays yours.
edits.after: Viktor is a monster if he free-scales, but you hold the pick initiative: your R range and fear open on him from angles his Gravity Field can't cover, and the fear cancels his Arcane Storm before it does work. Face him, hold your feared E for the storm, and blow him up before he kites. Deny his farm and the game stays yours.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Personal Space has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field (W): matchup-defining, 17s at rank 1 falling to 13 — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. - His Q shield cycles every 9-5s: poke in the gap between casts. - Your W (16s) answers exactly one commit; your R (140s) is for the moment it all goes right.

edits.after: Doom's empowered Q fears the immobile Viktor — he has no dash to break distance, so one feared bolt buys a free auto and E before he answers.

notes: Viktor's content layer used pre-rework names (Death Ray, Chaos Storm); kit authority is Hextech Ray (E) and Arcane Storm (R). tradeGood/dosFull assumed Viktor dashes — he has none, so Vex's mark-on-dash passive never procs off him; rewrote around his Q shield cycle instead. Level chart rows 4-6: content and packet said Vex, full said Skill/Skill/Viktor — moved full sides to Vex (win[N] already agreed, so side-only edits per the chart rule). Whether Arcane Storm counts as a cancellable channel post-rework was not verifiable from the kit text beyond its channel flag; kept the existing claim on that basis.
